name: Button
intent: Triggers an action. One primary Button per view.
usage: Use one primary per view. Use secondary for quieter paths, tertiary for low-emphasis actions, and danger only for work that cannot be undone. Accessibility is built in: native button, focus ring, loading and disabled states, and a label for icon-only buttons. See contracts/button.json for the full contract.

size.note: Heights 28 / 36 / 44 (control scale). Inside a ButtonGroup the group sets size. Without a size, a surrounding Density picks it: compact sm, default md, comfortable lg.

iconOnly.note: Square button. Requires label for a11y; label is visually hidden.

pressed.note: Toggle state for secondary and tertiary Buttons: brand tint and border, with aria-pressed. With aria-expanded (a button that shows or hides a panel, like the Toolbar Filters button) only the look changes.

useWhen: Submit, confirm, open, create, navigate to an action.
doNot: Do not use for in-text navigation (use Link).
Do not put two primary Buttons in one view.
a11y: loading sets aria-busy and aria-disabled, keeps width and full color, and ignores clicks. It does not look disabled.
iconOnly needs children as accessible label.
pressed sets aria-pressed, unless the Button already has aria-expanded.

examples.usage: Tab to the first button to see the focus ring.

items.caption: Tab here to see the focus ring

examples.title: Primary
examples.usage: Use one primary per view. Show sm, md and lg when hierarchy or density changes.

examples.title: Secondary
examples.usage: Use secondary for cancel, back, or other paths that should stay quieter than primary.

examples.title: Tertiary
examples.usage: Use tertiary for quiet actions in toolbars, empty states, or dense screens where a filled button would feel heavy.

examples.title: Danger
examples.usage: Use danger only for actions that cannot be undone, like delete. Ask the user to confirm when a mistake would be costly.

examples.title: With icons
examples.usage: Put an icon before the label to make the action clearer, or after it to show forward movement. Icon-only buttons still need a label for screen readers.

examples.title: Pressed
examples.usage: A toggle that stays on, like Filters while the filter bar is open.
